questionText:
Read the following case study on youth community mobilization and social development and answer the questions that follow:

A contingent of 50 college student volunteers from the National Service Scheme (NSS) organizes a 7-day residential community camp in an adopted rural village. Embodying the foundational NSS motto, 'NOT ME BUT YOU', the student volunteers collaborate with the local Gram Panchayat to address village development needs:
1. Shramdaan (Voluntary Physical Labor): Volunteers construct soak pits to manage stagnant wastewater around communal handpumps, preventing mosquito breeding.
2. Health and Nutrition Awareness: Volunteers conduct door-to-door surveys, screen children for growth faltering, and organize a street play (Nukkad Natak) on anemia.
3. Digital Literacy: Training rural women and farmers to operate UPI mobile payments and access Kisan Call Centre agronomic advisories.
4. Tree Plantation: Planting 500 indigenous fruit-bearing trees (neem, amla, jamun) along school boundaries. Through democratic teamwork, empathetic rural immersion, and civic service, student volunteers develop leadership resilience and social sensitivity.

topic: Child Protection Institutions and Statutory Functions
questionText:
Match the child protection institution in List I with its role in List II under the Juvenile Justice Act:

List I:
(A) Child Welfare Committee (CWC)
(B) Juvenile Justice Board (JJB)
(C) Specialized Adoption Agency (SAA)
(D) Observation Home

List II:
(I) Quasi-judicial district authority deciding care, protection, and rehabilitation of destitute/abandoned children
(II) Magisterial bench handling rehabilitation and inquiries concerning children in conflict with the law
(III) Recognized agency providing institutional care and processing legal adoptions for orphaned infants
(IV) Temporary facility for the safe custody and observation of a child in conflict with law during inquiry

options.text: An increase in the proportion and absolute number of elderly persons in the total population due to falling birth rates and higher longevity
